# Need, purpose and tentative domains

Candidate definition: a **need** identifies a condition or outcome that matters to an identified person or group in a context. A **purpose** explains why an activity or arrangement is worth pursuing. Whether and how needs, wants, goals and purposes should be distinct formal concepts remains open.

“Learning” or “health” alone names a concern without saying what is needed. “I need sufficient rest to sustain my daily activities” makes more of the need and context explicit. “I need a new app” may embed a premature solution choice; identify the desired outcome before assuming the app is required.

The assistant's **broad responsibility area/domain** proposal meant a heading such as health, finances or customer service that groups related needs. It was introduced too early and remains optional and unaccepted. A heading organizes retrieval; it does not establish a need or obligation.

An **ongoing obligation** was proposed as a responsibility that persists or recurs: paying employees each pay period, for example. Completing one payment does not end the continuing responsibility. Whether this requires a formal category is unresolved; see [actors and roles](actors-and-roles.md).

For authoring these descriptions, follow the accepted [problem/context and participant-language requirements](../../application/problem-context-and-actor-language.md). Their examples allow an opportunity or purpose as well as an observed problem; the conceptual distinctions below keep their existing standing.

Candidate need information: beneficiary or stakeholder; desired condition; motivating purpose; context; current shortfall; constraints and tradeoffs; whose judgment would establish improvement. Qualitative purposes such as curiosity and enjoyment need not be forced into scores. Inspiration can motivate exploration before a specific solution or requirement exists.

Requirements express conditions intended to help address needs; their adequacy requires justification under the accepted [requirements-to-needs rule](requirement.md#from-requirement-fulfillment-to-need-fulfillment). EOM-02 is resolved at that scope. EOM-07 and EOM-10 retain their recorded scope in [the ledger](../../../../source-locators.md#source-c43947fdcdae322a).
